llm.summary: This VMware audit and policy helper is coherent, but it needs review because a single environment variable can disable all policy checks for high-impact VMware operations.

dimensions.detail: The artifacts document VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as disabling all policy checks, including deny rules and maintenance-window enforcement, while the package is meant to guard high and critical VMware operations; no scoped approval, signed config, or per-operation control is documented for that bypass.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via uv package vmware-policy with a vmware-audit CLI; the inspected artifact contains markdown documentation only and no executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Auto-loading on VMware tool calls is broad, but it is disclosed as dependency behavior and vmware-policy itself exposes no MCP tools.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes persistent local audit records to ~/.vmware/audit.db with rotation and reads ~/.vmware/rules.yaml; this is expected for auditing, but logs can contain infrastructure parameters/results and redaction depends on tool authors marking sensitive parameters.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is a non-user-invocable infrastructure library and CLI for VMware audit logging, policy checks, input sanitization, and read-only gating across a VMware skill family; that purpose matches the documented capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing in production. Configure ~/.vmware/rules.yaml and read-only mode deliberately, protect ~/.vmware permissions, monitor audit entries with ok_bypassed status, and do not set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED except as a tightly controlled break-glass action.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The auto-load behavior is confirmed in SKILL.md, but it is consistent with a shared decorator/audit dependency and does not by itself create hidden execution or unrelated authority.
[SQP-2] expected: The bypass switch is confirmed in SKILL.md, capabilities, setup, and CLI docs; it is disclosed, but its all-policy scope is a material review concern for a high-impact VMware policy layer.
